companies.note: Full commercial C-suite is public on the company's own site. AlphaSense is one of the few names in this batch with a real CMO who owns brand outright, and she has taken two companies through an IPO brand-build — the exact motive a three-year sponsorship is sold against. No separately named EMEA president was found on a company page despite a large London presence; the approach runs through Zynczak with Kolstein on the commercial side.

people.name: Heather Zynczak
people.note: The buyer, and the brief's named contact — confirmed still CMO on AlphaSense's own author page and speaking as CMO on AlphaSummit 2026 material. Appointed April 2024. Prior CMO at Domo (brand launch, $0-100m) and at Pluralsight through its IPO; before that Oracle and SAP. Brand-build-for-an-IPO is her track record, which is the argument a multi-year sponsorship has to win.

people.name: Kiva Kolstein
people.note: Carries president as well as CRO, so he is the co-signer on anything sold as pipeline rather than brand. Ex-CRO at Handshake and Chief Growth Officer at Percolate.

people.name: Jack Kokko
people.note: Founder-CEO, the cheque signer. No motorsport tie found.

companies.note: Checked Also's own launch communications and the Rivian newsroom spin-out announcement: no marketing officer of any level is named publicly, and no CEO title is used either. The company is fronted by Chris Yu as co-founder and president, with Rivian founder RJ Scaringe as chairman of the board — so the approach is Yu direct, with Scaringe as the escalation. The brief's 'Undisclosed CEO' is right that no CEO is named, but the person to call is Yu, not a vacancy.

people.name: Chris Yu
people.note: The operating principal and the public voice of the brand — gives the interviews, presents the TM-B. Was Rivian's VP of Future Programs before the spin-out, so he owns product and brand together in the absence of a CMO. Company-owned leadership page could not be reached; title is consistent across the micromobility.io interview and Tech Brew's launch coverage.

people.name: RJ Scaringe
people.role: Chairman of the Board (Founder & CEO, Rivian)
people.note: Co-founder of Also and chairs its board; Rivian retains a significant minority stake. Any sponsorship of this size would be visible to him, and Rivian's own brand posture would set the tone.

companies.note: Checked Anduril's own leadership and news pages: there is no CMO. Marketing sits with Jeff Miller, hired in May 2024 as the company's FIRST marketing chief at VP level — a young function reporting into a defence company whose brand is run largely through comms and the founder. IMPORTANT CORRECTION for the brief: Palmer Luckey is the founder and public face but he is NOT the CEO — Brian Schimpf is co-founder and CEO. For a European motorsport programme the sharpest door is Richard Drake, who runs Anduril UK & Europe as a P&L.

people.name: Jeff Miller
people.note: Anduril's first-ever marketing chief (May 2024), from Cruise where he was VP marketing; before that senior director of marketing/creative at Snapchat, and PepsiCo and Ogilvy earlier. A consumer-brand builder inside a defence prime — the profile most likely to entertain a sponsorship. No company-owned page names him, so treat the seat as reported and re-confirm before an approach.

people.name: Matthew Steckman
people.note: The revenue owner — Anduril has no CRO; Steckman's remit explicitly covers business performance and revenue generation alongside corporate and divisional operations.

people.name: Richard Drake
people.note: The right entry point for anything European. Runs the UK and European business, which has grown from roughly 20 people to past 100. Ex-Babcock International, where he was Chief Executive of Mission Systems and Group CTO — a British defence-industrial operator who knows what a UK visibility platform is worth.

people.name: Brian Schimpf
people.note: The actual cheque signer, not Palmer Luckey. Luckey remains founder and the company's public personality (anduril.com/founders) and would carry the brand argument, but Schimpf runs the company.

companies.note: The strongest marketing setup in this batch: a full CMO who personally hosts the company's own media programme, sitting next to a president of worldwide field operations who has twice been a CRO at scale. The brief named no decision-maker for Armada — it is John Zissimos to call, Dan Wright to sign.

people.name: John Zissimos
people.note: The buyer. Named as CMO on Armada's own blog, where he hosts 'News from the Edge', the company's industry podcast — a marketing chief already investing in owned media and long-form brand storytelling, which is the disposition a three-year rights deal needs.

people.name: Tom Schmit
people.note: Commercial owner. Joined from AuditBoard where he was CRO and took ARR from $50m past $250m in four years; seven years before that at AppDynamics, also as CRO, through $50m to $500m+. Hospitality-and-pipeline arguments land with him.

people.name: Dan Wright
people.note: Founder-CEO and the cheque signer; fronts the company externally (e.g. the 'Arsenal of Democracy' appearance on Armada's own blog). No decision-maker was named in the brief — this is him.

people.name: Pradeep Nair
people.note: Ex-VP of Microsoft Azure. Relevant only if the pitch is a real edge-compute workstream at the track (trackside data, connected garage over Starlink — Armada already ships Starlink-backed edge units), in which case he is the counterpart who has to want it. Not confirmed on a company-owned page.

companies.note: Checked Baseten's own site: no CMO and no CRO are listed. Marketing is led at head-of-function level by Mike Bilodeau, with a separate head of product marketing under him and an open Executive Assistant to the Head of Marketing req — the function is real and growing but has no officer above it. An engineering-led company; the sponsorship argument has to be won with the founders, not delegated to a marketing department.

people.name: Mike Bilodeau
people.note: The marketing owner, named as Head of Marketing on Baseten's own author page. No officer sits above him, so he would build the case but Srivastava would decide it.

people.name: Tuhin Srivastava
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO. With no CMO or CRO in place he is both the cheque signer and, in practice, the buyer.

people.name: Amir Haghighat
people.note: The technical counterpart if the pitch is an inference workstream rather than a logo — Baseten's product is model inference, so any real team deployment (strategy modelling, telemetry inference) runs through him.

companies.note: A public company with a complete, individually-published C-suite — the cleanest decision path in this batch. Natalie Sunderland's mandate is written on Bloom's own page as building an iconic brand, which is as close to an invitation as this exercise gets. No EMEA or international president is named on the leadership page, so Europe would be argued through Joshi's commercial organisation.

people.name: Natalie Sunderland
people.note: The buyer, and an unusually good one: her published remit is strengthening market position, accelerating growth and 'building an iconic brand'. Over two decades in strategic marketing; came from Global Head of Marketing and Communications at BNY Mellon, where she owned global brand strategy for a sponsorship-heavy institution. Named one of Business Insider's Most Innovative CMOs for 2024.

people.name: Aman Joshi
people.note: Commercial owner. 22 years at GE across GE Aviation, GE Power, GE Capital and the Global Growth Organization, latterly global GM of GE's Aeroderivative units business — an industrial turbine executive, so the engineering-partnership framing of a power-unit-era F1 argument is native to him.

people.name: KR Sridhar
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still Founder, Chairman and CEO. Founded the company in 2001; previously director of the Space Technologies Laboratory at the University of Arizona working on Mars exploration systems. Note for timing: Simon Edwards became CFO in April 2026, so a new CFO is pricing multi-year commitments.

companies.note: Checked CodeRabbit's newsroom and its own Business Wire releases across 2025-26: a CRO was appointed but no CMO, VP marketing or head of marketing is named anywhere public. This is a sales-led company — the sponsorship case has to be made as go-to-market, to Mulqueen, with Gill signing. Worth noting the EMEA angle sits with the CRO, not a regional lead.

people.name: Matthew Mulqueen
people.note: The de facto buyer in the absence of a CMO — owns global go-to-market, sales and customer success, and is explicitly scaling regional teams across North America, EMEA and APJ. Personally led EMEA sales for both Datadog and AppDynamics through their IPO growth years, so a European rights platform is a familiar instrument. Appointed April 2026; previously CRO at LILT AI, with earlier roles at Kong and Cresta.

people.name: Harjot Gill
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still co-founder and CEO across the company's 2026 releases (including the $143m raise at a $1.5bn valuation in August 2026). With no marketing officer, he is the brand decision himself.

companies.note: Complete and current: a CMO who also owns the partner ecosystem, and a CRO appointed to accelerate growth. Both sit on Coralogix's own about page and blog. An Israeli-founded observability company with a US and European go-to-market — marketing and partnerships in one seat is useful, because a sponsorship can be argued as a partner-ecosystem platform rather than pure brand.

people.name: Brian Mullen
people.note: The buyer, and his remit covers the partner ecosystem as well as global marketing strategy — which is the lever for a hospitality-and-co-marketing case. Previously CMO at InfluxData, with senior go-to-market roles at Twilio and Nexus Venture Partners.

people.name: Chetan Chaudhary
people.note: Commercial owner, announced on Coralogix's own blog and introduced by Assaraf personally — hired explicitly to accelerate growth, so he is spending against pipeline.

people.name: Ariel Assaraf
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO and co-founder (founded 2014). No motorsport tie found.

companies.note: Checked corgi.insure, the company's YC profile and its own funding releases: Corgi publishes no leadership page and names no marketing or revenue officer. The named executives are the two founders plus function heads in government affairs and portfolio risk — an engineering- and underwriting-led company that has scaled to roughly 250 people without a marketing chief. The brief named no decision-maker; it is Nico Laqua, with Emily Yuan as the operating counterpart. Re-check before an approach: a company that quadrupled its valuation inside 2026 is exactly the kind that hires its first CMO at short notice.

people.name: Emily Yuan
people.note: The nearest thing to a commercial owner in the absence of a CRO or CMO — runs operations and does the company's external interviews. No marketing officer exists above or beside her.

people.name: Nico Laqua
people.note: The cheque signer and, with no CMO, the brand decision too. Also described as CTO in some records — a technical founder running the company. Corgi went from a $160m Series B at $1.3bn (May 2026) to $2.6bn weeks later and a further extension at $4.0bn in July 2026, so capacity is not the constraint; attention is. No company-owned leadership page exists, hence reported.

companies.note: Checked Crusoe's own leadership page and newsroom: the published C-suite is deep (president, COO/CFO, chief data centre officer, chief real estate officer) but there is NO chief marketing officer and no CRO. Marketing runs at VP level. For a sponsorship the real path is Lochmiller and Cavness — both founders front the company publicly and Cavness holds strategy — with Gordon pricing it.

people.name: Sharieff Mansour
people.note: The senior-most marketing person found; no CMO sits above him. Previously at RelationalAI, Microsoft and Orange. Sourced only from data-broker and LinkedIn records — no Crusoe-owned page names him — so confirm the seat before using it as the entry point.

people.name: Michael Gordon
people.role: Chief Operating Officer & Chief Financial Officer
people.note: Holds both operations and finance, so a multi-year commitment is priced by him. Came from MongoDB, where he was COO and CFO through its public-company growth — he will want the deal argued in payback, not exposure.

people.name: Cully Cavness
people.note: Moved to president and chief strategy officer when Gordon joined; owns long-term strategy and innovation programmes and is the founder who does most of the podcast and conference circuit — the most reachable senior door. Energy background: Petrie Partners, Recurrent Engineering.

people.name: Chase Lochmiller
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still co-founder and CEO. Ex-Polychain Capital general partner, quant researcher at Jump Trading and GETCO; Stanford CS (AI), MIT maths and physics.

companies.note: No CMO exists, but this is the one company in the batch where that does not matter: marketing and communications for Divergent sit with George Biggs, who spent nearly 13 years at McLaren Automotive and left as its Chief Sales & Marketing Officer. DEEP MOTORSPORT AND PERFORMANCE-AUTOMOTIVE TIES throughout — Divergent's DAPS platform supplies 3D-printed structural parts to McLaren (a multi-year partnership; the W1's titanium front suspension mirrors an F1 pushrod layout with inboard dampers), Bugatti (Tourbillon chassis and suspension), Aston Martin and Mercedes-AMG, and the group's own Czinger Vehicles builds record-setting hypercars. This is a company that already sells into the racing supply chain; a sponsorship conversation here is a supplier conversation, not a halo one. No company-owned leadership page was reachable, so the seats are reported from motorsport trade press and appointment coverage — confirm titles before an approach.

people.name: George Biggs
people.role: Chief Communications Officer, Divergent Technologies (Chief Commercial Officer, Czinger Vehicles)
people.note: THE call. Owns marketing and communications for Divergent while serving as CCO of Czinger Vehicles (appointed May 2025). Ex-McLaren Automotive Chief Sales & Marketing Officer and managing director for Asia-Pacific across nearly 13 years — he has sat on the manufacturer side of the McLaren brand and knows exactly what motorsport rights are worth and what they cost. The warmest leadership tie in this batch.

people.name: Lukas Czinger
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still co-founder and CEO in 2026 (LA500 2026 listing). Runs the end-to-end AI-design, additive-manufacturing and robotic-assembly platform; publicly fronts the technology story.

people.name: Kevin Czinger
people.note: Founder and the inventor behind DAPS; also CEO of Czinger Vehicles, the hypercar marque. The performance-brand instinct in the group is his — he built a car company to prove the manufacturing platform, which is the same logic that makes a racing programme legible to him.
